build: Provide the cuDSS 0.8 CUDA 12 wheel's include and lib directories, a complete CUDA header directory, and CUDA 12 cuBLAS and CUDA runtime libraries.
Run working_tests/benchmark_npf_coarse_direct.py --method cudss --cudss-bridge /tmp/libnpf_coarse_cudss.so with the desired case, level and output arguments.

methods.graph: Production line smoother with Warp CUDA graph capture.
methods.direct-single: Host SuperLU, with one direct correction at the parent of the coarse grid.
methods.cudss: Device CSR coefficient updates, FP64 cuDSS numerical LU and repeated solves in the Warp K-cycle graph. Same one-correction K-cycle as host LU.

cudss_notes: CPU builds the initial CSR index pattern and cuDSS performs host symbolic ordering. Coefficients, factors, right-hand sides, and corrections are device-resident. A scalar reports coefficient changes. The experiment recaptures the solve graph after numerical refactorization.
memory_notes: cuda_pool_high_bytes measures allocations through the Warp CUDA pool. cudss_allocator_peak_bytes tracks cuDSS allocation requests in its registered async allocator, excluding Warp's CSR and vector arrays. They are separate counters and are not additive.
timing_notes: The public solve time includes setup and GPU synchronizations. It excludes model build, external physical audit, and result saving. Backend time comes from the numerical solve loop and excludes reference and workspace setup. For repeated steady trials the report uses the median of independent processes.
acceptance_notes: All runs converged and passed the independent NPF physical audit. Head differences are from paired solver runs on identical input cases.
